effect_estimate.comment: Purely qualitative thematic findings from interviews; no quantitative point estimates or inferential statistics are reported.
effect_estimate.value: Qualitative — no numeric effect estimate reported. Stakeholders reported that existing sanitation laws (including the Public Health Act) cannot achieve compliance through top-down inspections alone due to inactive community-level D-WASH structures, institutional silos across regulators and municipal bodies, unfinalized statutory instruments for minimum pit-latrine standards, unplanned settlement layouts lacking truck access roads, water/electricity disruptions, and upfront household cost barriers. Institutional and administrative measures reported to improve on-site sanitation access, predictability, and affordability in George Compound include broadening Lusaka Water Supply and Sanitation Company's (LWSC) mandate to cover on-site sanitation, registering household pit latrines for scheduled desludging via small routine contributions, integrating on-site sanitation into LWSC's digital customer service and payment platform, early-stage subsidies, regulatory licensing/inspection of service providers, and bottom-up community participation.
